components.css: .ds-checks { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 264px; } .ds-check { font: 400 13px/1.45 system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; height: 26px; padding: 0 8px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: var(--text, #1f1f1f); cursor: pointer; text-align: left; } .ds-check:hover { background: var(--surface-2, #f1f3f4); } .ds-check[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--blue-tint, #e8f0fe); color: var(--blue-strong, #0b57d0); } .ds-check:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue, #1a73e8); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-num { display: inline-block; min-width: 28px; height: 20px; padding: 0 6px; border-radius: 6px; text-align: center; font: 600 12px/20px ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; background: var(--surface-2, #f1f3f4); color: var(--text-2, #5f6368); } .ds-check[data-state="ok"] .ds-num { background: var(--ok-tint, #e6f4ea); color: var(--ok, #137333); } .ds-check[data-state="warn"] .ds-num { background: var(--warn-tint, #fef7e0); color: var(--warn, #9a5300); } .ds-check[data-state="bad"] .ds-num { background: var(--bad-tint, #fce8e6); color: var(--bad, #c5221f); }

components.css: .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 74px 112px minmax(140px, 240px) minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(150px, 220px); column-gap: 14px; align-items: baseline; padding: 3px 14px; min-height: 24px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #e3e5e8); font: 13px/1.45 system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif; color: var(--text, #1f1f1f); cursor: pointer; } .ds-row:hover { background: var(--surface, #f8f9fa); } .ds-row:has([data-sev="bad"]) { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bad-tint, #fce8e6) 55%, var(--bg, #ffffff)); } .ds-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blue, #1a73e8); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-t { font: 12px ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", Menlo, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--text-2, #5f6368); text-align: right; } .ds-v { display: flex; gap: 7px; align-items: baseline; color: var(--text-2, #5f6368); } .ds-v i { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--ink); flex: none; } .ds-e { font-weight: 500; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-p { font: 12px ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", Menlo, monospace; color: var(--text-2, #5f6368); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-c { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-c[data-sev="bad"] { color: var(--bad, #c5221f); } .ds-c[data-sev="warn"] { color: var(--warn, #9a5300); } .ds-c[data-sev="note"] { color: var(--text-3, #6f7378); font-weight: 400; }

narrative.overview:
Pulsecheck is a DevTools panel that sits next to Elements and Network, so it borrows their material: white ground, cool grey surfaces separated by 1px hairlines, system sans at 13px, monospace for anything that is evidence. Google blue carries every action, selection and focus state. Green, amber and red appear only where a check has a result. Vendors get their own categorical palette, used on the pulse strip, the vendor chips and the swatch in each row.

The signature is the session pulse strip: a canvas timeline across the top where every event is a 3px bar, coloured by vendor and sized by source, with dashed page boundaries and finding marks under the baseline. Live checks sit to its right, and each count rolls when it changes. Clicking a count filters the table to the rows behind it. The table below is dense (24px rows), grouped by page under sticky headers, with a Check column that states each finding in plain words.

Density is the default. Decoration is limited to tonal fills, hairlines and the vendor swatches; there are no gradients, no illustrations inside the panel and no shadows on resting surfaces. Light and dark follow the DevTools theme.
keyCharacteristics: White first, cool grey tonal layers, 1px hairlines between every band.
One action colour (Google blue) for actions, selection and focus.
Semantic green, amber and red reserved for check results and finding rows.
A categorical vendor palette, separate from the semantic one.
Monospace with tabular figures for times, counts and payloads.
8px corners on every control; tonal fills instead of borders for on states.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means action, selection or focus. Nothing decorative is blue; a blue thing can be clicked or is the current selection.

rules.name: The Findings Own Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only where a check has a result: count badges, the Check column, finding row tints, strip marks and the capture error banner. Never use them for chrome or emphasis.

rules.name: The Two Palettes Rule
rules.body: Vendor colours identify the sender; semantic colours judge the event. A vendor swatch never carries a verdict and a verdict never takes a vendor colour.

rules.name: The Evidence Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything copied from the wire (timestamps, payloads, URLs, IDs, counts) is set in monospace with tabular figures. Prose and labels never are.

rules.name: The Chrome-Only Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Uppercase appears only in the table header: sans, 11px, 600, 0.04em tracking. No other label, page title or meta line is uppercase.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the layer floats over content and will go away. Bars, rows, chips, buttons and fields never cast one.

dos: Do use `blue` for one filled primary action per surface and `blue-strong` text for every other action.
Do separate bands and rows with 1px `line` hairlines and layer with `surface` and `surface-2`.
Do set times, counts, paths and payloads in monospace with tabular figures.
Do tie every semantic colour to a check result that a user can click through to rows.
Do show on states with a `blue-tint` fill and off states with an outline ring.
Do define every colour for both the light and the dark theme under the same token name.
donts: Don't use green, amber or red for chrome, emphasis or vendor identity.
Don't use vendor colours for anything other than strip bars and swatches.
Don't add shadows to resting surfaces; only popovers and tooltips float.
Don't use uppercase outside the table header, and never above 0.06em tracking.
Don't set any text below 4.5:1 against `bg` or `surface`; `text-3` is the floor of the text ramp, not a starting point for lighter greys.
